newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee races to sharply higher close.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee races to sharply higher close.

text.p: CSCE coffee staged a late- session rally to end sharply higher on Friday, as traders brushed aside talk of a bearish forecast for Brazil's 1997/98 crop.
The benchmark May contract shot up 5.75 cents per lb on the day, to close at 176.85, after matching a contract high set two days ago of 177 cents.
Traders said talk influential consultant Leon Yallouz had forecast next season's Brazilian harvest at around 27.5 million 60-kg bags initially deflated coffee prices this morning.
Yallouz would not comment on his report, which he distributes to private clients, but market participants here and in Brazil said they believed the 27.5 million figure was accurate.

After the initial pullback, speculative buyers returned to the market once May appeared to stabilize around 173 cents. Steady options-related buying also fueled the late run-up, traders said, noting keen interest in May out-of-the-money calls at 180 and 190 cents.
"The market keeps going up on its own momentum," said Smith Barney analyst Walter Spilka. "As long as it points higher it is going to continue to draw in speculators."

Traders also cited rumors, confirmed after the close of trading, that Colombia would raise its internal coffee price. Late Friday, Colombian coffee officials announced they had increased the internal price by 5.48 percent, to an all-time high of 327,250 pesos per 125-kg load.
Also after the close, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by a steep 11,250 bags overnight, or 43 percent, leaving 14,545 bags in the exchange's certified cache.
Based on today's performance, traders looked for the market to continue to work its way higher next week.
"The outlook continues to be positive," said one broker. "Origins don't have anything left to sell...We haven't seen the highs by any means."
Beyond the 177-cent mark, further resistance should emerge at 190 cents, followed by 200.00 ($2). Support was seen at 172.50 and at 169 cents.
Futures volume on the exchange reached an estimated 9,548 lots.
((-- W Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640))
